notes:
CIRCUIT: four identical op-amp stages (each op-amp has a single reactive feedback element bridged from its output back to its non-inverting input) whose outputs are summed through three 1K resistors onto one right-hand column. Sources: V-DC 5V (#6) top-left and I-DC 10A (#17) bottom-left, both returned to ground.

NET MAP
  0   = ground: GND #7,#8,#14,#16,#22,#23; bottom of V-DC #6; bottom of I-DC #17; and the inverting (lower, '-'-marked) input of every op-amp (#2,#11,#15,#21), each of which is drawn with a short stub down to its own GND symbol.
  n1  = right end of R#4, left lead of L#0 (the 1uH feedback loop), non-inv input of op-amp #3 - the y~299 rail at x 550..608 plus the x~568 riser.
  n2  = output of op-amp #3, right lead of L#0 (down the x~726 riser), left end of R#5.
  n3  = output of op-amp #2, right plate of C#1 (down the x~451 riser), left end of R#4.
  n4  = top of V-DC #6, left plate of C#1 (down the x~344 riser), non-inv (+, upper) input of op-amp #2 - the y~290 rail from x 233 to 366.
  n5  = inverting (lower) input of op-amp #3 -> down-left to (532,361) -> the long x~530 column -> corner at (543,709) -> left plate of C#20. Only 2 terminals, but that is what is drawn (see judgement call S25).
  n6  = summing column on the right: right end of R#5 -> (870,330) -> (870,455) -> (930,455) -> down the x~930 column, picking up the right end of R#10 at S29 (928,573) and the right end of R#19 at the bottom corner (930,700).
  n7  = output of op-amp #11, right plate of C#9 (down the x~793 riser at S28), left end of R#10.
  n8  = left plate of C#9 (up the x~661 riser at S24), non-inv input of op-amp #11, right end of R#12.
  n9  = output of op-amp #15 (up the x~426 riser at S27), right lead of L#13, left end of R#12 - the y~563 rail from x 426 to 556, passing UNDER the x~530 column.
  n10 = top of I-DC #17, left lead of L#13, non-inv input of op-amp #15 - the wire that runs right from the source at y~600, turns up at x~291 (S33) to the y~565 rail.
  n11 = right plate of C#20, left lead of L#18 (up the x~655 riser at S43), non-inv input of op-amp #21.
  n12 = output of op-amp #21 (up the x~777 riser at S41), right lead of L#18, left end of R#19.

JUDGEMENT CALLS
  * S25 (532,561) deg=4 - THE one real X crossing on this sheet. Called CROSSING. Evidence: the horizontal rail carries a small hand-drawn hop LOOP at (483..491, 559..569) - inkmap shows a ~9x11 px ring with a clear white hole at (487..488,562..563), i.e. a loop, not a solder dot (stroke width here is ~4 px and a dot would be solid). It is the only hop mark anywhere on the sheet (hop score 3.6; every other site scores 0.0), and this is the only place on the sheet where two wires actually cross in an X - every other intersection is a plain T. The loop sits ~47 px left of the crossing, which is a drafting offset (the drafter drew the rail with its hop, then placed the column slightly right of it); there is no other wire anywhere near x=485 for the hop to refer to. Both readings are electrically sane, so the ink prior + the drafter's single deliberate hop mark decide it. The other reading (junction) would have merged the x~530 column into the y~563 rail, putting op-amp #3's inverting input and C#20's left plate onto the same node as op-amp #15's output, L#13's right lead and R#12's left lead - one 5-terminal net instead of the 2-terminal n5 and 3-terminal n9.
  * B0 bridge (366,293)->(366,304) DROPPED. The tracer bridged op-amp #2's two input leads across an 11 px gap. inkmap at (366,299) shows two clean, separate horizontal strokes (rows 292-294 and rows 303-306) with 8 blank rows between them at x=350..380 - they do not touch. Keeping the bridge shorted the 5V source (6.0 and 6.1 both landed on net 0) and shorted op-amp #2's inputs together: electrically impossible.
  * All other CRITICAL sites (S2 344,292; S3 451,299; S4 568,299; S6 726,319; S24 661,559; S27 426,562; S28 793,564; S29 928,573; S33 291,596; S41 777,703; S43 655,713) are unambiguous T shapes - a wire run terminates on another run, no dot needed and no hop drawn. All confirmed JUNCTION from the 5x crops; no override was required, the explicit keys record that each was inspected.

PORT / PIN FIXES
  * #9 Capacitor t0: p1@(742,479) was a stroke of the handwritten '1uF' label brushing the top of the box (left it on a 1-terminal net n6). Repointed to p3@(740,504), the real right lead that runs right and down the x~793 riser to op-amp #11's output rail.
  * #14 GND t0: p0@(697,641) was the top of the handwritten '1uH' label below the symbol; the real terminal is the stem leaving the top of the box, p1@(674,585), which runs up to op-amp #11's inverting input. This also cleared the 1-terminal net n9 (op-amp #11's '-' input).
  * #20 Capacitor t1: p1@(595,742) was a stroke of the '1uF' label (1-terminal net n13). Repointed to p2@(554,712), the real left lead going left to the (543,709) corner of the x~530 column.
  * #21 Op-Amp pin order was scrambled: the tracer had t0(in+) on the OUTPUT lead p0@(739,724) and t2(out) on the lower input. Zoom at 9x shows the drawn '+' at (700,717) next to the upper input lead (y~712) and the drawn '-' at (701,728) next to the lower input lead (y~733), apex pointing right. Set t0=p1 (upper, +), t1=p2 (lower, -), t2=p0 (apex, out).
  * Op-amps #2, #3, #11, #15 were checked at 9x and the default order is right: '+' is drawn beside the upper input in all four (op-amp #3 shows only a '+' at (637,306), level with its upper input at y~304; no '-' glyph was drawn, so the lower lead is the inverting input by elimination). Note that this means every stage is drawn with its feedback element returning to the NON-inverting input - unusual, but that is unambiguously what is on the paper and GT describes the drawing.
  * Unused-port warnings on #4, #5, #12, #18, #19 are all strokes of the '1K/1uH' value labels touching the boxes; the real leads were already selected. Left alone.

CLASSES: no reclassification needed; every symbol matches its label.
UNRESOLVED: none. ERC clean, 24 components, 13 nets.
